solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Time to 'shuffle' Balls!

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
to waddle is to walk with a shuffling, rocking gait

explanation.surface: An order to make Ed Balls shuffle along, the politician being told his time is up.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks hint that 'shuffle' is a plain synonym here, not an anagram signal; Balls is a former Labour shadow chancellor.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls is slang for nonsense or rubbish talk, which is exactly what twaddle means.

clue.text: Labour result diabolical: has to accommodate Clegg's tail-enders

indicators.note: the tail-enders of a word are the letters at its very end, here the final pair
something diabolical is in a dreadful state, so the word beside it comes out jumbled
to accommodate is to take in and house, so one set of letters goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written before being rearranged
the last two letters of Clegg

explanation.surface: A political jibe: Labour's dire election result means it must make room for the tail end of Nick Clegg's Liberal Democrats.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour looks like the party, but it is the definition in its ordinary sense of hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: To labour is to work hard against difficulty, an everyday synonym for striving with effort.

clue.text: see 27ac.
Wearing empty codpiece, is inclined be a scrubber?

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its insides, keeping only its first and final letters
what is worn goes around the wearer, so the word that follows encloses the other

blocks.note: the first and last letters of codpiece
something that is inclined tilts or leans

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about a man in a hollow codpiece being tempted to behave like a slapper.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrubber is British slang for a promiscuous woman; the question mark flags that the definition takes it literally as one who scrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse something is to scrub it clean, so being a scrubber is cleansing taken literally.

clue.text: Having an erection finished off youth – dropped ball not treated properly

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so the named letter falls out of the word

blocks.note: slang for being aroused
something finished off is done
a youth is a boy
a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A lurid tale of an aroused youth who loses a ball and is badly treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hard done by has been unfairly or harshly treated, so the idiom matches the plain phrase.

clue.text: Nuts reversed on lads (they're fleshy and dark purple)

indicators.note: reversed means turned back to front, so the word before it is read from right to left

blocks.note: nuts means crazy
sons are lads

explanation.surface: Crude schoolboy humour about lads' bruised, swollen nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsons are small plums with juicy flesh and a deep blue-purple skin, a literal description.

clue.text: In the company of one royal familiarly getting end away enthusiastically

indicators.note: with its end taken away, a word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to be with someone is to be in their company
a means one
Wills is the popular nickname for Prince William

explanation.surface: Gossip about someone who spent time with Prince William and got their end away with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting your end away is British slang for having sex, which is the surface; here it simply cuts a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with a will means doing it eagerly and energetically, an idiom for wholehearted effort.

clue.text: Slight lust to get screwed after being elected

indicators.note: something screwed is twisted out of shape, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

blocks.note: a politician who has been elected is in
taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A cynical view of politicians, with a little lust getting satisfied once they are in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the elected piece first in the down entry, before the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight is a snub or affront, and an insult is a remark or act that offends, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: With drink around, one abandoned seat

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and uninhibited, so the letters run riot into a new order

blocks.note: a means one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk staggers off, leaving their seat empty with the drinks all around.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink is slang for the sea, so the definition is surrounded by water, not by alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship far from land has the ocean all around it, and 'the drink' is informal for the sea.

clue.text: Holly cut off small penis head and tackle?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, at the front

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the first letter of penis
rig and tackle are both equipment or gear

explanation.surface: A castration joke: a man named Holly has his meagre equipment chopped off.
explanation.walkthrough: Holly reads as a person's name, but it is the evergreen plant, and tackle is slang for male genitals.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small shoot or twig snipped from a plant, as used in Christmas decorations.

clue.text: Norm's getting in the drinks, as demonstrated by hypocritical 'family values' proponents

definitions.text: as demonstrated by hypocritical 'family values' proponents
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a norm is a standard; the 's is read as 'is'
doubles are large measures of spirits

explanation.surface: A man called Norm buys a round, with a jab at moralising politicians who preach one thing and do another.
explanation.walkthrough: Norm looks like a drinker's name, but it means a standard, which goes inside the drinks just before their final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying stricter moral rules to others than to oneself is the classic hypocrisy of preachers of virtue.

clue.text: Member needs to get someone to shag, which is a joke

blocks.note: a leg is a limb, or member
to pull is British slang for picking someone up for sex

explanation.surface: A man's member needing a partner is dismissed as laughable.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg-pull is a playful hoax or tease, an idiom from pulling someone's leg.

clue.text: see 26dn.
Tabloid coverage of Goth 'orgy' game-killer?

indicators.note: an orgy is a wild, disordered scene, so the letters are thrown into confusion
coverage wraps around its subject, so the tabloid encloses the other letters

blocks.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A red-top newspaper's lurid report of a Goth orgy that ended in a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: Game here is hunted birds and animals, so a game-killer is a gun used on a shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun is the firearm used to bring down game birds such as pheasant and grouse.

clue.text: (& 16ac.) Stiff tips which thwart advances

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the plural noun

blocks.note: a stiff is a corpse, so stiff means dead
tips are ends

explanation.surface: Firm tips that rebuff unwanted sexual advances.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead end is a road or line of enquiry going nowhere, so it blocks any progress forward.

clue.text: see 15ac.
Bloody awful! End Obama's dithering – top of list is replacing his no.1

indicators.note: the top of a word in a list is its first letter
replacing his first letter means the president's initial is swapped out for another
dithering is wavering back and forth, so the letters wobble into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before its first letter is swapped
the first letter of list

explanation.surface: An exasperated plea for Obama to stop dithering, with a list of priorities headed by replacing him.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloody is British slang used as an intensifier, so the definition is a strong expletive phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnable means dreadful or detestable, matching a vehement expression of how terrible something is.

clue.text: Shag gardener, somewhat shrunken

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of, so the letters sit within the words before

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A randy instruction to bed the gardener, who is rather shrivelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggard describes a gaunt, drawn, worn-out look, so a shrunken face fits it well.

clue.text: Nipples engulfing her bust possibly

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so the letters are smashed and reassembled
to engulf is to swallow up, so the first word surrounds what follows

blocks.note: paps is an old word for nipples or breasts
taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A breathless description of nipples on a woman's bust, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Bust looks like the body part matching the nipples, but it is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps and possibly are adverbs signalling uncertainty, interchangeable in nearly any sentence.

clue.text: Mary Whitehouse type of headline?

blocks.note: first meaning: one who bans things; Mary Whitehouse was a British campaigner against sex and swearing on television
second meaning: a headline running across the full width of a newspaper page

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the outraged headline a moral campaigner might provoke; the two parts are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A censor who prohibits things is literally one who bans, and a full-width front-page headline is also called this.

clue.text: Novel: Top Luge, which is full of goo

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the noun

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A review of a book called Top Luge that turns out to be sentimental slush.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like a book, but it is the signal; Top Gun is the film being sent up.
explanation.definitionFit: A gluepot is a pot for heating or holding glue, so it is literally full of a sticky substance.

clue.text: European area, one very into pisspoor lager

indicators.note: into puts one set of letters inside another
something piss-poor is badly made, so the letters end up out of order

blocks.note: a means one
V is the abbreviation for very
taken as written

explanation.surface: A British tourist abroad who is very keen on the dreadful local lager.
explanation.definitionFit: The Algarve is Portugal's southernmost region, a coastal holiday destination in Europe.

clue.text: Bear up, having extremely leaky passage

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top
the extremes of a word are its outermost letters

blocks.note: to lug is to carry or bear a heavy load
the first and last letters of leaky

explanation.surface: An uncomfortable image of someone straining to bear up while suffering a leaky back passage.
explanation.walkthrough: Bear looks like the animal, but it is the verb to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A gully is a narrow channel or ravine cut by water, a kind of passage through land.

clue.text: A bit of baby's malodorous crap

indicators.note: a bit of means a portion, so the letters are a run within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A smelly nappy, with a little of the baby's stinking mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Crap looks like the noun completing the nappy scene, but it is the slang adjective meaning very bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Crap as an adjective is slang for very poor quality, and abysmal means appallingly bad.

clue.text: Midas-like grip usually acquired by the fired top-level manager?

definitions.text: usually acquired by the fired top-level manager?
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun

blocks.note: King Midas turned everything he touched to gold
a handshake is a grip of the hand

explanation.surface: A jab at sacked executives who walk away with fortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: Fired sounds like baked in a kiln, fitting the gold, but means dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: A large severance payment given to a departing executive is known by this idiom, often criticised as rewarding failure.

clue.text: (& 13dn.) Blustered on, fly undone, revealing a rather susceptible body part

indicators.note: undone means unfastened and loose, so the letters come apart and regroup

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pompous man rants away, unaware his trouser fly is open and exposing him.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly undone suggests open trousers, but undone is the signal working on the fly with the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft underbelly is a vulnerable weak spot, literally the unprotected belly of an animal.

clue.text: (& 3dn.) Maybe George said it wasn't valued highly enough

indicators.note: said means spoken, so what matters is how the description of George is pronounced, not spelt

blocks.note: Prince George, a boy in the British monarch's family, is one example of the kind

explanation.surface: Someone called George grumbles that something was sold off too cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Mail is the British postal service; critics said its 2013 sale under Chancellor George Osborne was priced far too low, so George fits the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: The postal company's flotation price was judged far below its worth, and critics said it was undervalued.

clue.text: Lacking in a certain ministerial role, Portillo left out of reforms

definitions.text: Lacking in a certain ministerial role
definitions.note: a minister without portfolio lacks this

indicators.note: out means removed, so the named letter is taken away
to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: Michael Portillo is a former Conservative minister
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: Portillo is dropped from a reshuffled cabinet, left without any ministerial job.
explanation.walkthrough: A minister without portfolio sits in cabinet with no department, so the definition describes what such a minister lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is the set of responsibilities held by a government minister, such as a department.
